objectives: Survey dark matter evidence + candidates + experiments.
Trace dark energy discovery + equation of state.

slides.title: Dark matter: evidence, candidates, direct + indirect searches
slides.body:
**Dark matter (DM)**: non-luminous, non-baryonic matter that interacts gravitationally but only weakly (if at all) electromagnetically. Comprises ~26% of cosmic energy density; ~85% of all matter; ~5× baryon density.

**Evidence — six independent lines**:

**1. Galactic rotation curves**:
- **Vera Rubin + Kent Ford** (Carnegie/DTM, 1970s): measured rotation velocities of stars + gas in spiral galaxies (M31, M33, etc.). Found flat rotation curves (v ≈ const at large r) instead of Keplerian v ∝ 1/√r expected from visible mass.
- v² ≈ GM(r)/r ⇒ M(r) ∝ r ⇒ ρ(r) ∝ 1/r² → invisible 'dark halo' extending well beyond luminous disk.
- Rubin's 1980 PRL was definitive; she should have shared the Nobel.

**2. Galaxy cluster dynamics**:
- **Fritz Zwicky** (Caltech, 1933): measured velocity dispersion of galaxies in Coma Cluster; applied virial theorem → required ~400× more mass than visible. Coined 'dunkle Materie' (dark matter). Dismissed for decades; fully vindicated post-1970s.

**3. Gravitational lensing**:
- **Strong lensing** (Einstein ring; arc systems like Abell 370, 2218): cluster mass from arc positions far exceeds baryonic content.
- **Weak lensing** (statistical shape distortions of background galaxies): cosmic shear; KiDS, DES, HSC, Euclid 2023.
- **Bullet Cluster** (1E 0657-56; Clowe et al. 2006): two colliding clusters; X-ray gas (most baryons) shocked + lags collision center; weak-lensing mass map peaks ahead of gas — DM passes through (collisionless), gas does not. **The cleanest empirical signature of DM** — disfavors modified-gravity-only alternatives.

**4. CMB acoustic peaks**:
- Heights of 1st + 3rd peaks vs 2nd in Planck spectrum encode Ω_b vs Ω_DM at recombination. Ω_DM h² = 0.120 (Planck 2018); ~5× Ω_b h² = 0.0224.

**5. Large-scale structure**:
- Galaxy clustering, weak lensing, BAO: matter power spectrum P(k) requires Ω_m ≈ 0.31; baryons alone insufficient. N-body simulations (Millennium, IllustrisTNG, ABACUS) with cold DM reproduce observed cosmic web; DM-free models fail.

**6. BBN consistency**:
- BBN constrains baryon density Ω_b independently of CMB. Both give Ω_b ≈ 0.05 — much less than total Ω_m ≈ 0.31.

**DM candidates**:

**WIMPs (Weakly Interacting Massive Particles)** (Lee + Weinberg 1977): m ~ 100 GeV-TeV; cross-section ~ weak scale → thermal relic abundance naturally Ω_DM ≈ 0.26 ('WIMP miracle'). Predicted by SUSY (neutralino) + extra dimensions.
- **Direct detection**: nuclear recoil from WIMP-nucleus scattering. Underground cryogenic detectors (deep mines, low background). LUX (2013-2016) → LZ (LUX-ZEPLIN, SURF Sanford SD, 2024 results): 7 tonne Xe TPC; cross-section limit σ_SI < 9.2×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at m = 30 GeV. XENONnT (Gran Sasso, Italy): 8.5 tonne. PandaX-4T (China). DAMA/LIBRA annual modulation (NaI, 12σ signal, controversial; ANAIS + COSINE-100 dedicated tests). DarkSide, DEAP (Ar TPCs). No detection above background; WIMP parameter space squeezed.
- **Indirect detection**: DM annihilation/decay products (γ-rays, e⁺, ν). Fermi-LAT, AMS-02, IceCube, HESS, CTA. Galactic center excess (Fermi); anomalous positron excess (PAMELA 2008, AMS-02 confirmed). Interpretation contested (millisecond pulsars vs DM).
- **Collider**: missing transverse momentum at LHC. No clear signal at √s = 13.6 TeV.

**Axions** (Peccei + Quinn 1977; Weinberg + Wilczek 1978): pseudo-scalar field originally proposed to solve strong-CP problem in QCD. Mass m_a ~ µeV-meV; couples weakly to photons (axion-photon coupling g_aγγ).
- **ADMX** (Axion Dark Matter eXperiment, Univ Washington): tunable microwave cavity in strong B field; converts axions to photons (Sikivie effect). KSVZ + DFSZ models; probing meV mass range.
- **HAYSTAC, CAPP, ABRACADABRA, DMRadio**: complementary mass ranges.
- **Helioscopes** (CAST → IAXO): solar axion conversion.
- **Stellar cooling bounds** (red giants, WD, SN1987A): constrain g_aγγ.

**Sterile neutrinos** (right-handed; no SM gauge interactions): m ~ keV. Decay → X-rays. 3.5-keV X-ray line (Bulbul + Boyarsky 2014, controversial; XRISM 2024 follow-up).

**Primordial black holes** (PBH): formed from large primordial perturbations. LIGO BH-BH mergers + microlensing constrain. PBH window 10⁻¹⁶-10⁻¹¹ M⊙ remains open.

**MACHOs** (massive compact halo objects: brown dwarfs, planets, BHs): excluded as dominant DM by microlensing (EROS, MACHO, OGLE).

**Self-interacting DM** (Spergel + Steinhardt 2000): solves small-scale structure issues (missing satellites, too-big-to-fail, core-cusp); σ/m ~ 0.1-1 cm²/g.

**Fuzzy / ultralight DM**: m ~ 10⁻²² eV; de Broglie wavelength ~kpc scale; quantum-pressure halo cores.

**MOND (Modified Newtonian Dynamics)** (Milgrom 1983): modify gravity at acceleration a₀ ~ 10⁻¹⁰ m/s²; explains galaxy rotation curves without DM; struggles with clusters + CMB + Bullet Cluster.

**Status**: DM as a particle is the dominant paradigm; null direct/indirect/collider results continue to pressure WIMPs but axions + sterile ν + PBHs viable. Future: LZ → DARWIN/XLZD (~50 tonne Xe); ADMX-EFR + DMRadio; CTA gamma-ray; SKA + 21cm; JWST + Euclid LSS.

slides.title: Dark energy: 1998 discovery + equation of state + DESI
slides.body:
**Dark energy (DE)**: smooth (non-clustering), negative-pressure component driving accelerating expansion. Ω_DE ≈ 0.69; w ≈ -1.

**1998 discovery — two competing teams**:

**Supernova Cosmology Project (SCP)**: Saul Perlmutter (LBNL Berkeley) + team. Years of high-z Type Ia SNe surveys with 4m telescopes (CTIO, AAT, KPNO, ESO) + spectroscopy with Keck. Published Perlmutter et al. 1999 ApJ.

**High-z Supernova Search Team (HZT)**: Brian Schmidt + Adam Riess (then at UC Berkeley) + collaborators. Riess et al. 1998 AJ.

Both teams independently found: high-z (~0.5) Type Ia SNe ~25% dimmer than expected for Ω_m = 1 decelerating universe → universe accelerating expansion → DE.

**Type Ia SNe as standardizable candles**:
- White dwarf in binary accretes from companion until reaching Chandrasekhar mass (~1.4 M⊙) → thermonuclear runaway → C/O fusion to Ni-56 → peak luminosity from radioactive decay.
- 'Standardizable' via Phillips relation (1993): brighter SNe have wider light curves; correction to ±0.15 mag → M_B ≈ -19.3.
- d_L(z) from m - M comparison; sensitive to integrated H(z).

**Nobel 2011**: Perlmutter + Schmidt + Riess.

**Equation of state w**: p_DE = w·ρ_DE·c². ΛCDM has w = -1 exactly (constant). Allowed values:
- w = -1: cosmological constant Λ (Einstein 1917).
- -1 < w < -1/3: quintessence (dynamical scalar field).
- w < -1: phantom (violates dominant energy condition) → Big Rip.
- w > -1/3: not accelerating.

**Parameterizations**:
- **Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL)**: w(z) = w₀ + w_a·z/(1+z). DESI 2024 hint of w₀ ≈ -0.6, w_a ≈ -1.4 (preliminary; 3-4σ deviation from w = -1).
- **w-w_a**: same as CPL.
- **Equation of state from scalar potential**: V(φ); various functional forms.

**Dark energy probes**:

**Type Ia SNe**:
- **Pantheon+** (2022): ~1700 SNe to z ~ 2.
- **Union3** (2023): meta-analysis.
- **DES-SN5YR** (2024): ~1500 DES SNe; precision DE constraints.
- **JWST** (2024+): high-z SNe Ia + Cepheid recalibration; Riess 2024 H_0 ≈ 73 → 70 with JWST.
- **Future**: Roman 2027, Vera Rubin LSST 2025-2035; precision w(z).

**Baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO)**:
- Sound horizon r_s ≈ 150 Mpc (set by recombination) imprinted on galaxy clustering at all redshifts.
- 'Standard ruler': measures angular distance D_A(z) + Hubble parameter H(z).
- **BOSS** (2010-2014, SDSS-III): LRGs, ELGs, quasars at z = 0.2-0.7.
- **eBOSS** (2014-2019, SDSS-IV): out to z = 2.5.
- **DESI** (Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument, Kitt Peak, 2021-2026; first results Apr 2024): 5000 fiber spectrograph; ~30 million galaxies + quasars. April 2024 BAO + SNe joint fit: 2.5σ-3.9σ hint of w deviating from -1; w₀ ≈ -0.6, w_a ≈ -1.4 — 'dynamical dark energy' hint.
- **Euclid** (ESA, launched July 2023; first data 2025): photometric + spectroscopic; 1.5×10⁹ galaxies; BAO + weak lensing.
- **Roman** (NASA, 2027 launch): wide-field IR; high-z SNe + cosmic shear.

**Weak lensing**:
- **KiDS, DES, HSC**: σ_8 + S_8 constraint; mild tension with Planck (2-3σ).
- **Euclid + Roman + LSST**: precision shear + photometric BAO.

**Cluster counts** (Planck-SZ, eROSITA): mass function tail; sensitive to σ_8 + dark energy.

**Cosmological constant problem**:
- Naive QFT vacuum energy ~Planck scale: ρ_vac ~ (10¹⁹ GeV)⁴ → Λ should be ~10¹²² × measured.
- SUSY (m_SUSY ~ TeV) reduces to (TeV)⁴ → still ~10⁶⁰ × off.
- Observed Λ ≈ (2.3 meV)⁴ — unnatural in any standard QFT framework.
- **Resolutions**:
  - **Anthropic** (Weinberg 1987): Λ > observed prevents galaxy formation → no observers; landscape (multiverse) selects.
  - **Modified gravity**: f(R), Horndeski, DGP, massive gravity.
  - **Dynamical Λ** (quintessence, k-essence, phantom).
  - **Backreaction** of inhomogeneities (Buchert; controversial).
  - **Holographic / emergent**: Verlinde 2010 emergent gravity.
  - **Refined swampland conjectures** (de Sitter, Trans-Planckian): de Sitter may be metastable in string landscape.

**Status**: ΛCDM with w = -1 fits all data within current precision; DESI 2024 first hints of dynamical w. Future BAO (Euclid + DESI + Roman) + LSST + CMB-S4 will measure w(z) to ~1% precision, decisively discriminate Λ from quintessence.

slides.title: Cosmic energy budget + the three-component universe
slides.body:
**Cosmic energy budget today (Planck 2018 ΛCDM)**:

  **Ω_Λ ≈ 0.685** (dark energy / cosmological constant)
  **Ω_DM ≈ 0.265** (cold dark matter)
  **Ω_b ≈ 0.049** (baryonic matter — protons, neutrons, electrons)
  **Ω_r ≈ 9.2×10⁻⁵** (photons + neutrinos)
  **Ω_k ≈ 0** (curvature; flat)
  **Total ≈ 1** (flat universe)

Of the ~5% baryonic matter:
- **Stars + ISM + WHIM** (warm-hot intergalactic medium): ~0.5%.
- **Diffuse gas (most of baryons)**: ~4.5%; finally detected by fast radio burst (FRB) dispersion measures (Macquart et al. 2020) — closed the 'missing baryon problem'.

Of the ~26% dark matter:
- Distributed in halos around galaxies + clusters; cosmic web filaments.
- N-body simulations (Millennium 2005, ABACUS 2024) predict 'NFW' profile ρ(r) ∝ 1/(r·(1+r/r_s)²) (Navarro-Frenk-White 1996) at large radii.
- Sub-halo mass function: ~10³-10⁴ subhalos > 10⁷ M⊙ in Milky Way; matches observed satellite count after baryonic feedback.

Of the ~69% dark energy:
- Smooth on observable scales (does not cluster); spatially uniform.
- Equation of state w ≈ -1 (with current precision ~5%).
- Pressure p_Λ = -ρ_Λ c²; sources accelerating expansion since z ≈ 0.6.

**Compositional evolution over cosmic history**:
- **Inflation epoch** (~10⁻³⁶ to 10⁻³² s): inflaton energy dominates; ~10¹⁵-10¹⁶ GeV scale.
- **Reheating** (~10⁻³² s): inflaton → SM particles; T ~ 10¹⁶ GeV.
- **Radiation era** (10⁻³² s to ~50 kyr; z > z_eq ≈ 3402): Ω_r dominates.
- **Matter era** (50 kyr to ~10 Gyr; z_eq > z > z_Λ ≈ 0.3): Ω_m dominates.
- **Λ era** (z < 0.3, ~10 Gyr to ∞): Ω_Λ dominates; accelerating.

**'Cosmic coincidence' problem**: Why does Ω_Λ ≈ Ω_m today, when both evolved differently throughout cosmic history (Ω_m a⁻³ vs Ω_Λ const)? Equality happens within factor ~2 of present epoch — bizarre coincidence unless explained anthropically.

**Six-parameter ΛCDM precision (Planck + BAO + SNe + lensing)**:
- ω_b = 0.02237 ± 0.00015
- ω_c = 0.1200 ± 0.0012
- 100·θ_MC = 1.04092 ± 0.00031
- τ = 0.054 ± 0.007
- ln(10¹⁰ A_s) = 3.044 ± 0.014
- n_s = 0.965 ± 0.004
- → H_0 = 67.36 ± 0.54 km/s/Mpc (Planck-only)
- → σ_8 = 0.811 ± 0.006
- → t_0 = 13.797 ± 0.023 Gyr

**Connection to all cosmology lessons**:
- **CMB + recombination**: peak positions + heights fix Ω_b, Ω_DM, Ω_Λ via acoustic physics.
- **Friedmann + expansion**: H(z) controlled by composition.
- **Inflation + early universe**: provides initial conditions (n_s, A_s) + flatness.
- **Structure formation + BAO**: DM seeds collapse; BAO probes H(z) + D_A(z) over expansion history.
- **Modern frontier**: H_0 + S_8 tensions hint that simple ΛCDM may need extensions (early DE, dynamical w, light relics, decaying DM).

**The dark universe is the central mystery of modern cosmology**: ~95% of the energy is in forms invisible to standard model probes. Whether these are: (a) novel particles + Λ; (b) modified gravity; (c) emergent phenomena from quantum gravity; (d) something else — remains the central problem of physics for the 21st century. The next decade (DESI, Euclid, Roman, LSST, CMB-S4, LiteBIRD, LZ → DARWIN, ADMX-EFR) is positioned to either confirm ΛCDM at percent precision or discover new physics.

question.question: Estimate DM density from rotation curve
question.goal: A galaxy has flat rotation v = 220 km/s out to r = 50 kpc. Estimate enclosed mass + average DM density assuming spherical halo.

steps.prompt: Write v² = GM(r)/r + solve for M(r) at r = 50 kpc.

acceptedAnswers: M(r) = v²·r/G; with v = 2.2×10⁵ m/s, r = 50 kpc = 1.54×10²¹ m: M ≈ 1.1×10⁴² kg ≈ 5.6×10¹¹ M⊙

steps.prompt: Compute average DM density assuming spherical halo.

acceptedAnswers: V = (4/3)π·r³ ≈ 1.5×10⁶⁴ m³; ρ_avg = M/V ≈ 7×10⁻²³ kg/m³ ≈ 0.05 M⊙/pc³ (or in GeV/cm³: ρ ≈ 0.04 GeV/cm³ avg, ~0.4 GeV/cm³ at solar position)

steps.reveal: V = (4/3)π·r³ = (4/3)π·(1.54×10²¹)³ ≈ 1.53×10⁶⁴ m³. ρ_avg = M/V ≈ 7.3×10⁻²³ kg/m³. Convert: ρ ≈ 0.04 GeV/cm³ (averaged). Local solar-neighborhood DM density (NFW peaked): ~0.3-0.5 GeV/cm³ (direct-detection input). The Milky Way virial mass ~10¹² M⊙.

steps.prompt: If DM is WIMPs at m = 100 GeV, how many WIMPs/cm³ locally?
steps.reveal: n_WIMP = ρ_local/m_WIMP ≈ 0.4 GeV/cm³ / 100 GeV ≈ 4×10⁻³ /cm³ ≈ 4000/m³. WIMP wind velocity ~220 km/s relative to Earth. Flux ~ n·v ≈ 8×10⁵/cm²/s. Cross-section σ ~ 10⁻⁴⁷ cm² (LZ limit) → rate per nucleus ~10⁻⁵⁰/s; needs tonnes of Xe + years of running to see a few events. LZ + XENONnT + DARWIN are pushing into this regime.

steps.prompt: Why is the Bullet Cluster (1E 0657-56) the cleanest DM evidence?

acceptedAnswers: Lensing mass peaks offset from X-ray gas (most baryons); shows DM passed through collision while gas shocked + lagged

steps.reveal: Bullet Cluster (Clowe et al. 2006): two galaxy clusters mid-collision. X-ray gas (Chandra) shows shock fronts where gas lags behind. Weak-lensing mass map (HST + Magellan): peaks aligned with galaxy distributions, OFFSET from gas. Most of baryonic mass is in gas; the larger mass component (gravitational lensing) is the DM — which passed through collision because it's collisionless. Hard to explain with modified gravity (modified-gravity should track baryons). Strongest empirical signature of DM as a separate component.

question.question: Why are LZ + XENONnT direct-detection null results making the WIMP paradigm increasingly difficult?
options: WIMPs (m ~ 100 GeV, σ ~ weak-scale) were favored by 'WIMP miracle' — natural thermal relic abundance matches Ω_DM ≈ 0.26. Lee + Weinberg 1977; SUSY neutralino canonical. Predicted nuclear-recoil cross-section σ_SI ~ 10⁻⁴³-10⁻⁴⁷ cm² for spin-independent scattering. **LZ 2024** (LUX-ZEPLIN, 7-tonne Xe TPC, SURF Sanford SD): σ_SI < 9.2×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² at m = 30 GeV — orders of magnitude below SUSY predictions for standard WIMP masses. **XENONnT** (Gran Sasso, 8.5-tonne) similar. **PandaX-4T** (China). No detection. Combined with: (a) null collider missing-MET searches at LHC; (b) null indirect detection (Fermi-LAT, AMS-02); (c) increasingly tuned SUSY parameter space; (d) approaching 'neutrino floor' (coherent ν-nucleus scattering background) — the WIMP paradigm is increasingly constrained. Alternative candidates (axions, sterile ν, ultralight, PBHs) becoming more attractive. Future DARWIN/XLZD (~50-tonne) + ADMX-EFR + DMRadio + CTA continue the search.
question.explanation: LZ 2024 + XENONnT + PandaX-4T cross-section limits σ_SI < 10⁻⁴⁷-10⁻⁴⁸ cm² rule out large swaths of natural SUSY WIMP parameter space. Null collider + indirect-detection + approaching ν-floor constrain WIMP paradigm. Axions, sterile ν, ultralight DM, PBHs gain attention. Future DARWIN/XLZD + ADMX-EFR push deeper.

slides.workedSolution: LZ 2024 + XENONnT + PandaX-4T (Xe TPCs) push σ_SI < 9×10⁻⁴⁸ cm² — far below natural SUSY WIMP predictions. Combined with collider + indirect-detection null results + approaching neutrino floor, WIMP paradigm increasingly constrained. Axion + sterile ν + ultralight + PBH alternatives gain attention; DARWIN/XLZD + ADMX-EFR continue the search.

question.question: ADMX-EFR (2030s) reports a 5σ axion detection at m_a = 5 µeV with KSVZ coupling.
question.prompt: What does this imply for the strong-CP problem + Peccei-Quinn symmetry breaking? How does it affect interpretations of the 3.5 keV X-ray line + ultralight DM models? Implications for DM-direct-detection community (WIMP vs axion) + future experiments? Discuss connection to inflationary axion cosmology + isocurvature perturbations.

question.question: Write the CPL (Chevallier-Polarski-Linder) parameterization of dark-energy equation of state.
question.hint: Two parameters: w_0 today + w_a slope; standard parameterization for evolving DE in DESI, Euclid, Roman analyses.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, summarize the cosmic energy budget + the 'dark universe' problem.
question.rubric: Mentions: Planck 2018 ΛCDM gives Ω_Λ ≈ 0.685 (dark energy), Ω_DM ≈ 0.265 (cold dark matter), Ω_b ≈ 0.049 (baryons), Ω_r ≈ 10⁻⁴ (photons + ν), Ω_k ≈ 0 (flat). About 95% of energy is in unknown forms. DM evidence: Zwicky 1933 Coma virial; Rubin 1970s flat rotation curves; Bullet Cluster 2006 lensing-gas offset; CMB peak heights; LSS + BAO; BBN. Candidates: WIMPs (LZ/XENONnT/PandaX null), axions (ADMX), sterile ν, PBHs, MOND alternative. DE: Perlmutter-Schmidt-Riess 1998 SN Ia accelerating expansion; Nobel 2011. w ≈ -1; DESI 2024 hints of w₀ ≈ -0.6, w_a ≈ -1.4 dynamical. Cosmological constant problem: naive QFT ~10¹²² × observed Λ. Anthropic, modified gravity, swampland alternatives. The 'dark universe' is the central problem of 21st-century physics; next decade (DESI, Euclid, Roman, LSST, CMB-S4, DARWIN, ADMX-EFR) will decide ΛCDM vs new physics.
